explanation: He had analysed seismic data, sending sound waves into the ground to find oil. Cher's 1998 hit 'Believe' turned Auto-Tune's robotic vocal effect into a pop sound.

claims.text: Before creating Auto-Tune, Andy Hildebrand worked in oil exploration, interpreting seismic data.
Hildebrand's earlier career was not in space flight, medical scanning or car making.
Seismic exploration sends sound waves into the ground and analyses their echoes to locate oil and gas.
Cher's 1998 song Believe made Auto-Tune's robotic vocal effect famous.
